title: Writing Your Own Functions
summary: Turn an expression you use often into your own SQL function.
intro: You have already used dozens of built-in functions. When the same expression keeps showing up in your queries, give it a name once with CREATE FUNCTION and call it like any built-in.
setup:
CREATE TABLE products (id integer, name text, price numeric(10, 2), category text);
INSERT INTO products (id, name, price, category) VALUES
    (1, 'Stapler', 12.50, 'Office'),
    (2, 'Desk lamp', 34.99, 'Home'),
    (3, 'Notebook', 4.25, 'Office'),
    (4, 'Coffee mug', 9.00, 'Kitchen'),
    (5, 'Water bottle', 18.75, 'Kitchen');

steps.title: A function for an expression
steps.body:
This lesson uses one table, `products`:

```sql harness
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products CASCADE;
{{code}}
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE products (id integer, name text, price numeric(10, 2), category text);
-- (1, 'Stapler', 12.50, 'Office'), (2, 'Desk lamp', 34.99, 'Home'), ...
```

You already know three families of built-in functions: math (`round`, `ceil`, `abs`), text (`upper`, `trim`, `replace`), and dates (`extract`, `to_char`, `age`). When you keep writing the same expression, name it with your own function:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION with_tax(price numeric) RETURNS numeric
    LANGUAGE sql
    RETURN round(price * 1.08, 2);
```

The parentheses list each parameter with its type, `RETURNS` gives the type of the answer, `LANGUAGE sql` says the body is SQL, and `RETURN` is the expression to compute. Call it like a built-in: `SELECT with_tax(10);` gives `10.80`. Like most built-ins, a NULL argument gives NULL.

The function is saved in the database, so creating it again fails:

```text
ERROR:  function "with_tax" already exists with same argument types
```

Every run in the editor starts from a fresh database, so this only happens when one program creates the same function twice.

example.title: Prices with tax
example.prompt: Create a with_tax function that adds 8% tax and rounds to cents, then show each product's price with tax.
example.output:
CREATE FUNCTION

     name     | price | with_tax
--------------+-------+----------
 Stapler      | 12.50 |    13.50
 Desk lamp    | 34.99 |    37.79
 Notebook     |  4.25 |     4.59
 Coffee mug   |  9.00 |     9.72
 Water bottle | 18.75 |    20.25
(5 rows)
example.explanation: `CREATE FUNCTION` prints its command tag and saves `with_tax`. The SELECT then calls it once per row, passing that row's `price` as the parameter. Inside the function, `price` means the parameter, so `round(price * 1.08, 2)` turns 34.99 into 37.79.

practice.title: Sale prices
practice.prompt:

1. Create `discounted(price numeric, percent integer)` returning numeric: the price with `percent` percent taken off, rounded to 2 decimal places.
2. Select `name`, `price`, and `discounted(price, 15)` as `sale_price` from `products`.
3. Sort by `id`.

hints: Taking 15% off leaves 85% of the price, so multiply `price` by `(100 - percent)` and then divide by 100.
Multiply by `price` before you divide. `(100 - percent) / 100` on its own is integer division and gives 0. Wrap the whole expression in `round(..., 2)`.

steps.title: Text functions and defaults
steps.body:
A function can return text too. Declare `RETURNS text` and build the answer with `||` or `format()`:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION label(name text, price numeric, currency text) RETURNS text
    LANGUAGE sql
    RETURN name || ' (' || currency || price || ')';
```

`DEFAULT` gives a parameter a value to use when a call leaves it out: with `currency text DEFAULT '$'`, `label('Mug', 9.00)` means `label('Mug', 9.00, '$')`. Parameters with defaults go last.

To change a function that exists, use `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` with the same name and parameter types. You can change the body or add defaults, but not the return type or the parameter names. The gotcha: a different list of parameter types, even one extra parameter, makes a second function with the same name instead of replacing the first. A call that fits both then fails:

```text
ERROR:  function label(text, numeric) is not unique
```

So settle the parameter list first, and use defaults to keep calls short.

example.title: Price labels
example.prompt: Create a label function, replace it with a version where currency defaults to '$', and call it with and without a currency.
example.output:
CREATE FUNCTION

CREATE FUNCTION

       us_label        |         eu_label
-----------------------+--------------------------
 Stapler ($12.50)      | Stapler (EUR 12.50)
 Desk lamp ($34.99)    | Desk lamp (EUR 34.99)
 Notebook ($4.25)      | Notebook (EUR 4.25)
 Coffee mug ($9.00)    | Coffee mug (EUR 9.00)
 Water bottle ($18.75) | Water bottle (EUR 18.75)
(5 rows)
example.explanation: The first version needs all three arguments. `CREATE OR REPLACE` keeps the same parameter types, so it replaces the body and adds the default instead of making a second `label` (its tag is still `CREATE FUNCTION`). `label(name, price)` fills in `'$'`, while `label(name, price, 'EUR ')` passes its own currency.

practice.title: URL slugs
practice.prompt:
Fix a slug function so it turns product names into clean URL names, then call it with and without a separator.

1. Keep the first version of `slug` from the starter.
2. Use `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` to redefine `slug(title text, sep text DEFAULT '-')` returning text: trim the title, replace each space with `sep`, and lowercase the result.
3. Select `name`, `slug(name)` as `slug`, and `slug(name, '_')` as `file_name` from `products`.
4. Sort by `id`.

Expected output:

```text
CREATE FUNCTION

CREATE FUNCTION

     name     |     slug     |  file_name
--------------+--------------+--------------
 Stapler      | stapler      | stapler
 Desk lamp    | desk-lamp    | desk_lamp
 Notebook     | notebook     | notebook
 Coffee mug   | coffee-mug   | coffee_mug
 Water bottle | water-bottle | water_bottle
(5 rows)
```
practice.starter:
-- First version: no trimming, no lowercasing, and sep is required
CREATE FUNCTION slug(title text, sep text) RETURNS text
    LANGUAGE sql
    RETURN replace(title, ' ', sep);

-- TODO: replace slug so it trims and lowercases, with sep defaulting to '-'

hints: Nest the built-ins from the inside out: `trim` the title first, then `replace` the spaces, then `lower` the result.
Put the default in the parameter list of the new version, like `sep text DEFAULT '-'`, and keep the parameter names `title` and `sep` the same as the first version.

recap:
- `CREATE FUNCTION name(param type) RETURNS type LANGUAGE sql RETURN expression;` names an expression.
- Call your function in SELECT like a built-in, once per row.
- `RETURNS text` makes a function that builds text.
- `DEFAULT` fills in a parameter the call leaves out. Defaults go last.
- `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` changes a function with the same parameter types. Different types make a second function.
